[.wrap-names,cols="2,2,4,2,5,3",options="header"]
|===
|Family |Target |Linked |Default |Why |Tested by

|AES-GCM
|emscripten
|BearSSL
|BearSSL
|the only AEAD backend there: webcpp does not build OpenSSL for Emscripten; size and speed not measured yet
|`+default_bearssl+`

|AES-GCM
|wasip2, wasip3
|BearSSL, with or without OpenSSL
|BearSSL
|constant time by design (link:https://www.bearssl.org/constanttime.html[BearSSL, constant-time crypto]), where OpenSSL is built no-asm and its AES and GHASH are table-based (link:https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/master/INSTALL.md[OpenSSL's INSTALL.md, no-asm])
|`+default_bearssl+`, `+default_both_wasm+`

|AES-GCM
|wasip2, wasip3
|BearSSL and OpenSSL, with `+WEBCPP_CRYPTO_DEFAULT_BACKEND_OPENSSL+`
|OpenSSL
|the program's choice
|`+default_openssl_wasm+`

|AES-GCM
|native, Clang and GCC
|OpenSSL, with or without BearSSL
|OpenSSL
|OpenSSL's assembly uses the CPU's AES and carry-less multiplication instructions on x86-64 and ARMv8 (link:https://github.com/openssl/openssl/tree/master/crypto/aes/asm[OpenSSL's AES assembly for ARMv8 and x86-64]; link:https://github.com/openssl/openssl/tree/master/crypto/modes/asm[OpenSSL's GHASH and AES-GCM assembly]); BearSSL has them on x86 only (link:https://www.bearssl.org/support.html[BearSSL, the AES implementations it selects]); speed not measured yet
|`+default_both+`

|AES-GCM
|native, MSVC
|OpenSSL, with or without BearSSL
|OpenSSL
|the same rule as with Clang and GCC, but here OpenSSL is built no-asm: table-based AES and 4-bit GHASH, no AES-NI, not constant time (link:https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/master/INSTALL.md[OpenSSL's INSTALL.md, no-asm]); where timing attacks matter, link BearSSL and define `WEBCPP_CRYPTO_DEFAULT_BACKEND_BEARSSL`
|`+default_both+`

|AES-GCM
|native
|BearSSL and OpenSSL, with `+WEBCPP_CRYPTO_DEFAULT_BACKEND_BEARSSL+`
|BearSSL
|the program's choice, constant time by design (link:https://www.bearssl.org/constanttime.html[BearSSL, constant-time crypto]): on MSVC, where OpenSSL is built no-asm, the choice for code that timing attacks threaten
|`+default_selected+`

|AES-GCM
|native
|BearSSL alone
|BearSSL
|the backend that is linked
|`+default_bearssl+`

|AES block cipher
|native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten
|any backend
|none
|a raw block cipher is a building block a program chooses deliberately, naming its backend; `aes256<>` takes AES-GCM's default as its argument, and its `make` does not compile where that is BearSSL
|`+default_selection_bearssl+`

|secp256k1
|native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten
|libsecp256k1
|libsecp256k1
|the only backend (link:https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1#readme[libsecp256k1's README])
|`+secp256k1+`
|===
